items.title: Pay the claimed amount (Mahnbescheid)
items.quote: Der Betrag ist bis zum 15.01.2027 zu zahlen.
items.computation: The letter states a fixed calendar date for payment: 15.01.2027. This is only 7 days after the 'Erlassen am' date of 08.01.2027, which is inconsistent with the statutory two-week Widerspruchsfrist (§ 692 ZPO) that a genuine German Mahnbescheid must grant before a Vollstreckungsbescheid can even be requested — a strong sign this is not a genuine court document and the printed date may not reflect any real legal deadline. Taking the letter at face value, the due date as printed is 2027-01-15.

warnings: This document has strong hallmarks of a scam/fake collection letter disguised as an official German court 'Mahnbescheid': payment is demanded directly into a private law firm's account ('Kanzlei Brandner Forderungsservice') rather than to the actual creditor, and the letter explicitly refuses payment to the court itself ('Zahlungen an das Gericht werden nicht angenommen') — a real Mahngericht does not collect or forward money at all.
The IBAN given for payment (DE10 7005 0000 0044 7120 91) fails the standard IBAN checksum validation, meaning it is misprinted or fabricated — do not transfer money to it.

The 7-day payment window (Erlassen 08.01.2027, due 15.01.2027) is far shorter than the statutory two-week Widerspruchsfrist required before a Vollstreckungsbescheid can be sought in a genuine German Mahnverfahren (§ 692 ZPO), and the letter contains no Widerspruch/objection instructions or form, which a genuine Mahnbescheid is legally required to include.
The underlying claim is for a contract with an 'Online-Spielothek Ltd.' (online gambling site) — such debts are a common pretext in German collection-letter scams.
The letter uses high-pressure language ('ohne weitere Anhörung', 'der Gerichtsvollzieher wird beauftragt') typical of scam dunning letters to rush payment before the recipient can verify it.

Recommend the recipient independently verify this Geschäftszeichen and the sending court directly via the official court's published contact details (not the phone/email printed on this letter) before taking any action or paying anything.
